reason: Conversation 1 kept power-off boundaries, guided the owner to the drum/belt/brush checks, correctly identified the charred short brush as the likely cause, advised replacing the pair matched to the motor label, added sensible commutator and connector checks, and set clear stop/escalation points if the burning smell returned or new brushes didn't restore drive. Conversation 2 over-reacted to a one-off faint smell from weeks ago by issuing a full 'stop using it' order (the ground truth has no critical stop), repeated itself, never got the owner to inspect the brushes, and ended with only a vague engineer referral, so it neither diagnosed nor gave part advice despite the fault being a cheap DIY brush swap.
